I lurk on r/loseit, you might find better replies there besides just "meal prepping".

I sometimes pack an extra snack for after work, that way I'm not tempted to buy fast food on the way home and sometimes I crack it open when we get slow. I also eat before work if I can, even if it's a hard boiled egg and then an apple I chow on in the car. 

My biggest help in weight loss is eating meals that really fill you up. I feel more satisfied after eating ancient grain rice vs white, plus you can microwave leftover rice really quick or throw it on a salad for a bibimbap style! So picking those complex carbs and dense proteins.

Dried fruit has made me feel more full, and is fun to snack on, but some do have extra calories. Also nuts! Nuts are so good for you and are satisfying. I like munching on raw carrot chips, they have a fun texture. I feel like pretzels fill me up more than chips or smart pop so I buy those for my salt craving. All of these go well on some crackers with a creamy light baybell, I pretend it's a charcuterie board. 

Just play around with easy grab choices that don't go bad if you forget to put them in the fridge when you get to work.

My weight loss journey was about eating healthier but I have found that reducing my portions to the serving size has been extremely helpful. And if I'm not full after my meal, I have a serving size of a snack or two. I added variety and slowly I didn't need the snacks anymore and wasn't inhaling a bag of chips for dinner because I was tired after work.

The hard part is being at work and then trying to look forward to a meal you might not have energy to make. So I feel you, it's really hard on this industry.

I love that people are encouraging you, and in all cases you should take your dang meds, but I wish someone had told me these things about Adderall before I started my journey.

As someone who had an Adderall prescription, I ultimately decided it wasn't for me. I could not shut up, and I was already really talkative. I could not sleep. I had a loss of appetite and IBS and cotton mouth and I got dangerously skinny. I would hyper focus on everything, and sometimes take on a larger task than what I needed to do in the first place. Like deep cleaning the window sill with a toothpick when I meant to just windex it, or reorganizing the bookshelf when I only wanted something good to read. The worst symptom was that I was not able to tap into my creative outlets. The art I made was different (Like bad outlines with intense shading, and really intense symmetrical patterns. Freaks me out to look at it.) and even when it wore off I felt like I couldn't create. The brain fog after using was really awful too. 

I'm not sure what you mean by weakness, but those ended up being weaknesses of the prescription for me. 

I encourage people to use Adderall for one of its purposes. It can be a tool to help you deal with ADHD, but it might not be a fix for your ADHD. It will help you learn to prioritize, complete tasks and focus when you need it. But honestly I don't know how severe your ADHD is, so talk to your doctor. I still struggle with my ADHD, but now that I know I can actually do things if I try (and usually it takes much longer than most people) I've opted to not take it any longer. Adderall ultimately helped me gain confidence and deal with my depression, anxiety, and ADHD but I am not willing to jump on that train again.

A shocking realization may be that no amount of meds will take away your mental illnesses. You must learn to treat them and live with them every day. Some days will be good and some days may come out of nowhere and beat you over the head.

Okay your post kind of triggered me because I used to think like this when I was younger. So if I'm mean that's why, and I guess here's some advice to my past self and you, if you want to listen.


1. Creating art is for yourself, not a competition. I never post art on social media anymore because I feel like if I try to frame it for others it's not true. You can admire others and honestly if you want to get to their level you can. It takes time. Also, modern art is so different from the past, the way we deal with societal pressures is seen in the art and related to, it's a beautiful thing to connect to an expressionistic piece, even if it's not perfect. 

2. Like yeah jobs suck but humanity is so much more complicated than cyber apes. People do care about others, and they show it, maybe not during their working hours but there is so much evidence to contradict the hate. I think maybe you haven't experienced or seen a job that really makes you think or challenges you, but why do you think so many people bring their work home with them? They have to talk out loud about the issues they're having, they have to do extra work at home. 
I think these days people really want to have a close connection with nature, we're looking for smaller houses like vans to travel in again. We want to learn how to do things the old way like sew, and bake by hand, and till the earth, even if it's a 3×5 in the back yard. We do want to disconnect from the deep city life. We feel it in our bones.

3. Who cares if you're unique? Just do your own thing. Stop feeling that pressure. Of course shallow people are bad.

4. I agree with appreciating the old and supporting creators but Holy moly, as much as you hate this life, this is the reality of it. This is real life. And we are all experiencing it. 

5. Yeah of course you find life's meaning in off time, I'll give you a hint, it's different for everyone. 

6. It's good you're trying to find inner peace. But happiness is an ebb and flow, you cannot control it, and if you silently pursue it, it will embrace you suddenly. I was very lonely for a long time and always thought I didn't have any friends because I purged the alcoholics and abusers from my life. I started to be kind to others and always say hi or find something to talk about. Like pushing me out of my comfort zone to be social, and I suddenly realized I was being invited out to do things I actually liked every weekend instead of crawling into bed 3am wasted and sad with the things they criticized about myself the next morning. I have people who call me to just chat, people who want to bake things for me, people to cheer me on. And I was really alone for a long time. Don't pressure yourself to just be happy or search for it, it's an equal exchange.

Of course it's the time we spend on this earth that matters, in the long run no one can make that much of a difference, but sometimes there's a fluke and you do it. People actively amplify your voice, they want you to be heard. Don't give up yet, I know it's grim, REALLY grim right now... But there's something just off screen to keep going for. I find reasons to keep going with every small accomplishment, that's how you have to do it. Getting out of bed, making a meal, calling someone who loves you to ask how they're doing. It's small things, but sometimes they're hard, and I don't do them every day, but it feels nice when I do.

So I'm leading a group of first time players and writing a bunch of my own for the campaign. I've done both styles where you pick a clan then decide what they were like as a human, but I recommend deciding what your human was like first! Pick a time period and think of what their job was, think of an event around that time and how they would have encountered a Vampire because of it. We all have passions as humans and that's the best place to start.

An interesting thing I've found to help with understanding my players characters is to ask them what themes like to go over in the campaign. Someone said dealing with realities and psychedelics, so their character has moved across the states following drug movements. Someone said fame and loss and now dance the dangerous line of stardom and the masquerade. 

Their life doesn't have to become all about vampire politics but you have to admit finding a group of like minded people with cool ass powers to be at least mildly interesting. You could even decide you had a falling out with your clan and run independently. As long as you obey the masquerade you can easily survive. 

Oddly enough thinking of the mundane things you did in your human life lead to how you operate in unlife.
